chapter_theme: The sun of the cosmos (அண்டாதித்தன்): the sun and the gods circle Meru in worship of the Lord's feet, and the Lord himself stands as the sun, the source of all lives, figured in a diagram of circles and petals; the way the sun travels beneath the earth is hidden from all but those who know.
structure_note: Praise of the sun as worshipper and as the Lord (1975 to 1978), the sun's diagram of triangles, circles and petals (1979, 1980), and the hidden way of the sun beneath the earth (1981 to 1984). The next chapter turns to the sun in the body.

1975.reading: The reason the gods, the red-rayed sun first among them, circle cloud-topped Meru is their tapas of bowing to the twin feet of the Lord, light of all lights, as their own light.
1975.nuance: The sun's daily round of Meru, an astronomical fact in Puranic cosmology, is read as circumambulation in worship. எஞ்சுடர் may be 'all lights' or 'the light that remains'; either way the sun's light is borrowed from the Lord's.

1976.reading: The sun, the holy Lord who stands as refuge for all lives, rising so that the seven worlds flourish without strife, is the origin of all lives.
1976.nuance: பகலவன் மாலவன் may name the sun and Vishnu side by side, or call the sun 'the great one'. The verse does not say plainly whether the புண்ணிய நாதன் is the sun or the Lord who stands as the sun; the chapter's drift favours the second.

1977.reading: The sun, with love and a thousand names, stands as the radiant light within the light; whatever the Vedic priests ask and the gods say, this is how love ripens toward the First One.
1977.nuance: ஆயிர நாமமும் (a thousand names) recalls the hymns of a thousand names. The last two lines can be read as 'whatever they ask, it is love that ripens', setting love above ritual request, but the syntax is loose.

1978.reading: He himself stands to the world as its principle, as the woman, as Shambhu, and as the cool light.
1978.nuance: தானே opens every line. தையல் (the woman) is Shakti and சம்பு is Siva, so the one who stands as the sun holds both. தண்சுடர் (cool light) is the moon, a surprise in a sun chapter: the Lord is both lights.

1979.reading: Triangle, circle, hexagon, two balanced circles, the pure eight, and in the outer circle sixteen petals: the sun rose in this distinct order.
1979.nuance: The verse describes a diagram (yantra) for the sun, or the centres of the body in yogic reading. வவைய is probably a misprint, perhaps for வளைய; துலை and மலைவுற்று are unclear.

1980.reading: Within the sun, in the triangle, the good sun shines as four; the sun is in the eight; and in the light's spreading it is sixteen.
1980.nuance: The numbers continue 1979's diagram and are often taken as the sun's kalas. கேத முறுங்கேணி is obscure: கேணி (well) and கேதம் (grief) give no clear sense here.

1981.reading: With the sun the earth went dark; the four that were divided babbled and passed away; you do not see the Vedic truth that stands within the light and beats like a drum.
1981.nuance: பேதித்த நாலும் may be the four Vedas, the four religions or the four states; துடியிடை (drum-waisted) is also an epithet of a woman. The plain sense is a reproach: the truth is in the light, and talk misses it.

1982.reading: The way the sun comes beneath the earth is a rare thing no one can see; the one who rises between water and fire is the sun beyond everyone's reach.
1982.nuance: Plainly the sun's passage under the earth at night. Symbolically the earth, water and fire are taken as centres of the body, so the hidden sun is the inner light rising in yoga. Both readings stand.

1983.reading: Cleaving the earth and what is below it, cleaving the sky and making space, cleaving the eye and giving bliss, he stood suited to the reckoned day.
1983.nuance: இடந்து (cleaving, digging through) repeats. கிழமை may be the day of the week, named after the sun, or 'what is rightfully his'. Line 1 is a foot short.

1984.reading: No one knows the way the sun comes cleaving the earth; those of the rare final texts say it circles the holy mountain where the brave one sits; those who knew the town knew and remained.
1984.nuance: அருங்கடை நூலவர் (those of the rare final books) may be Vedantins or Agama teachers. The mountain is Meru, or in yogic reading the head. ஊர் (the town) may be the Lord's abode or the body.

links.note: Both open on the sun's hidden road under the earth (பகலோன் வரும்வழி) and say no one knows it; 1984 adds what the learned say, that it circles the mountain, and that those who know the town know.

1981 says the world's divided talk babbles and passes while the truth in the light goes unseen; 1986, in the body's sun, says those who find where the sun settles still all that babble with it. Same words, பேதித்து and பிதற்று.

1975 says the sun and gods circle Meru (மேரு வலம்வரு) as tapas, bowing to the Lord's feet. 2465 has the yogi think on Meru with the disc of spreading rays (மேருவினோடே விரிகதிர் மண்டலம்) and gain Siva's grace by tapas. Meru and the sun's disc serve in one as cosmic worship and in the other as the yogi's object of contemplation.

1976 calls the sun (பகலவன்) the holy Lord who is refuge and origin of all lives. 2533 names பகலோன் இறையவன், the sun as the Lord of many ages. Both identify the sun with the Lord rather than treating it as a lesser god.

270 says love and Siva are not two (அன்பே சிவம்). 1977 says that whatever the Vedic priests ask and the gods say, this is how love ripens toward the First (ஆதியில் அன்பு பழுக்கின்ற வாறே). 1977 gives love the same final place as 270, set against ritual request.

Both verses open every line with தானே: in 10 the Lord is earth, sky, fire, sun and moon and the lady who pours rain (தையலுமாய்); in 1978 he is the world's principle, the woman (தையலுமாய்), Shambhu and the cool light. The near-repeat of form and figure places the sun chapter's Lord in the opening invocation's.

1980 says the sun shines as four in the triangle and as sixteen (சோடசம்) in its spreading. 853 says the unchanging sun takes in all sixteen kalas (கலைமுற்றும் ... ஈரெட்டு) when fire joins. Both give the sun the sixteen kalas usually the moon's.

1983 has the Lord cleaving earth, sky and eye (மண்ணை இடந்து, விண்ணை இடந்து) and giving bliss. 1984 says no one knows the way the sun comes cleaving the earth (பாரை இடந்து). The shared verb shows 1983's cleaving one to be the sun of 1984.

source_issues: 1979: வவைய is probably a misprint, perhaps for வளைய.
1980 line 3 (கேத முறுங்கேணி) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1983: line 1 (மண்ணை இடந்துஅதின் கீழொடும்) seems a foot short.
